userStories.title: Image limits and validation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Publish shared image input types, limits and deterministic validation from nax-agent.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

**Approach** — Limits live in nax-agent (`packages/nax-agent/src/session/image-input.ts`, exported from `.`), so feature 2 uses the same numbers:

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` | `["image/png", "image/jpeg", "image/gif", "image/webp"]` | accepted `mimeType` values |
| `MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE` | `10` | images on one `send` |
| `MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS` | `5_242_880` | per image, base64 length (5 MiB encoded = 3.75 MiB raw) |
| `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES` | `20` | images in one model request (whole history) |
| `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS` | `20_971_520` | base64 chars of images in one model request, and of one `send` |
| `IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE` | `1_600` | compaction estimate per image |

`validateImageAttachments(images: readonly ImageAttachment[]): string | undefined` returns `undefined` for a valid list, otherwise a one-line reason. Checks run in this order and the first failure wins:

1. the list length is over `MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE`;
2. per image, in list order: `mimeType` not in `IMAGE_MIME_TYPES`; `data` empty; `data` not matching `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$` or its length not a multiple of 4; `data.length` over `MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`; `width` or `height` present and not a positive integer;
3. the sum of `data.length` over the list is over `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`.

Because one valid `send` holds at most `MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE` (10, below `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES`) images totalling at most `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`, the request budget below never drops an image of the turn being sent. Pixel dimensions are not read from bytes here (feature 2 reads file headers).

`SendInput = { readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[] }` is declared in `image-input.ts`.

AC7 uses MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS + 4 characters (a multiple of 4), so it passes the base64 checks and fails only the per-image size check; keep the stated validation order.

**Scope** — In: new image-input module and tests; re-export ImageAttachment through cost/standard-types.ts; named exports of ImageAttachment, SendInput, validateImageAttachments and all six constants from src/index.ts; regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt with bun run api:update. Out: facade enforcement (US-003), native behavior/config mapping (US-004), request capping (US-005), compaction (US-006), file storage (US-007/008), ACP (US-009). Resizing, cropping or re-encoding images, and reading pixel dimensions from image bytes (feature 2 reads headers).

**Interface** — `validateImageAttachments(images: readonly ImageAttachment[]): string | undefined`; `SendInput = { readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[] }`. ImageAttachment is the single nax-ai type, imported via the allow-listed `src/cost/standard-types.ts` re-export, not a duplicate local interface or another direct nax-ai import. Write failing bun:test cases before implementation, including imports from the public entry.

userStories.title: Image input on the session facade
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add image send input and a capability query to the facade without breaking existing session objects or turn claiming.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

**Approach** — `AgentSession.send(message: string, input?: SendInput)`. Refusals are thrown synchronously, before a turn is claimed, in this order: the existing closed / busy / configuring checks; then `validateImageAttachments` failing → `AgentSessionError` code `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_INPUT` with the reason as message; then a non-empty `images` on a backend with no `acceptsImages` → `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` with context `{ capability: "images" }`.

`claimTurn` carries the images to `ctx.adapter.sendTurn(handle, message, { ...opts, images })`. `SendTurnOpts` gains `images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`; the key is present only when the list is non-empty.

`OpenedBackend` gains optional `acceptsImages?(): Promise<boolean>`.

`AgentSession` gains **optional** `acceptsImages?(): Promise<boolean>` (optional like `configure?` and `runCommand?`, so the existing hand-built `AgentSession` objects in nax source and tests still typecheck). The facade (`FacadeAgentSession`) always implements it: rejects with `AgentSessionError` `AGENT_SESSION_CLOSED` on a closed session; resolves `false` when the backend has no `acceptsImages`; otherwise resolves the backend's answer.

Do not await a capability answer in send or convert send to an async generator: only a missing backend method is the synchronous capability refusal. A backend reporting false still handles its own model/agent refusal during the turn. Carry images through claimTurn, runTurn and the private sendTurn wrapper while retaining the existing markTurn/event/cancel/single-use semantics.

**Scope** — In: session/agent-session.ts, agent-session-turn.ts, agent-session-types.ts, session-backend.ts, session-types.ts and agent-session-errors.ts; new facade image tests; regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt if declarations change the snapshot. Out: shared validation implementation (US-002), native capability and seeding (US-004), budgets/compaction/storage (US-005–008), ACP implementation (US-009). UI capability gates belong to feature 2.

**Interface** — `send(message: string, input?: SendInput): AsyncIterable<SessionEvent>`; `acceptsImages?(): Promise<boolean>` on AgentSession and OpenedBackend; `images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]` on SendTurnOpts; AgentSessionErrorCode gains `"AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_INPUT"`. Use fake backend sendTurn recordings and the shared session helpers in bun:test. Prove synchronous refusal before iteration and old-code failure before implementation.

userStories.title: Native turns send images
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let native sessions report image input support and seed validated images into model turns while refusing unsupported current-turn input.

**Motivation** — Today a user message is a plain string at every layer: nax-ai `ConversationMessage` role `user` has `content: string` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/types.ts`), `toPiMessages` pushes that string (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`), `AgentSession.send(message: string)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts`), and the ACP client sends one text block (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn.ts` `promptOnce`). Nothing can carry a picture.

**Approach** — `NativeSessionAdapter.imageInput(handle): Promise<boolean>` resolves the handle's model exactly as `sendTurn` does and returns whether its `input` includes `"image"`.

Native: `() => adapter.imageInput(handle)`. This is the native OpenedBackend's optional acceptsImages implementation.

Native `sendTurn` with non-empty `opts.images` on a model whose `input` lacks `"image"` throws `NaxError` code `NATIVE_IMAGE_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED` (context `stage: "native-session"`) before any model call and before any transcript save. Otherwise the turn seed is `{ role: "user", content: prompt, images }`. A `before_turn` handler's seed patch still replaces the whole seed (images included), as it does for the prompt today.

nax-agent's `CatalogModelOverride` gains `input?: ("text" | "image")[]`, and `toProviderOverrides` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/models.ts`) forwards it only when declared.

Resolve model and reject unsupported image input before entering runNativeTurn, whose caught error path persists a transcript. Keep the direct adapter no-save contract separate from the facade's existing turn-marker writes. No/empty images omit the seed's images key. Absent ResolvedModel.input is unknown and treated as text-only. Use the existing _clientDeps.build seam and withDerivedStream helper so the production streamComplete route is exercised while recording the client's requests.

**Scope** — In: native/session-adapter.ts, native/session/turn-loop.ts, session/native-backend.ts, config/catalog-overrides.ts, native/models.ts; new adapter images test and added provider-overrides.test.ts cases, leaving existing assertions unchanged. Integration tests must drive createAgentSession over nativeBackend for image send and acceptsImages. Out: facade declarations (US-003), request budget (US-005), compaction (US-006), sidecar storage (US-007/008), ACP (US-009), nax schema (US-010). History images after a native switch to a text-only model under `carryHistoryAcrossModels`: pi-ai itself replaces them with the text "(image omitted: model does not support images)"; nax adds nothing. Feature 2 shows its own notes.

**Interface** — `NativeSessionAdapter.imageInput(handle): Promise<boolean>`; native OpenedBackend `acceptsImages?(): Promise<boolean>`; `CatalogModelOverride.input?: ("text" | "image")[]`. runNativeTurn consumes the existing SendTurnOpts.images and seeds a user ConversationMessage. Model parsing remains parseNativeModel(handle.modelDef?.model ?? "") and client.model(provider, model), shared with sendTurn. Prove regression tests fail against old code before implementing.

userStories.title: Native request image budget
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bound native wire-request images by newest-first count and byte budgets without modifying saved history or dormant array identity.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

**Approach** — `capRequestImages(messages)` shapes the wire copy only. When no image needs dropping it returns **the input array itself** (same reference), so the existing "no clone when dormant" identity in `test/unit/native/session/loop-events/transform-context.test.ts` still holds. Otherwise it returns a new array and never changes the input array or its messages, so the saved transcript keeps every image.

It walks images from the newest message to the oldest, and within a message from last to first. It keeps an image when the kept count is below `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES` **and** the kept base64 total plus this image's `data.length` is at most `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`; otherwise it drops it. Count and size are checked together per image, so a dropped large image does not stop a later smaller one from being kept. A dropped image is removed from that message's `images` and the line `[image from an earlier turn dropped from context: <mimeType>]` is appended to that message's `content` (joined with `\n`). A message left with no images loses its `images` key.

It runs inside the native `request` wrapper in `turn-complete-step.ts` (reached through `completeWithRecovery`), on `wire.messages` from `applyHistoryPatch`, immediately before `deps.complete`; so it also bounds a `transform_context` handler's patch. Dropping an old image changes the request's prefix, so a prompt-cache prefix and the compaction anchor's `promptTokens` can be stale for that request; this is accepted (the anchor is an estimate already).

Every note line this feature appends to a user message's `content` (`[image from an earlier turn dropped from context: ...]`, `[image: ...]`, `[image missing]`) is appended once per image, in image order, joined to the existing `content` with `\n`; when `content` is empty the first line is used with no leading `\n`.

Because one valid `send` holds at most `MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE` (10, below `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES`) images totalling at most `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`, the request budget below never drops an image of the turn being sent. Pixel dimensions are not read from bytes here (feature 2 reads file headers).

**Scope** — In: create native/session/image-context.ts and image-context.test.ts; integrate the request wrapper; use US-002's MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES=20 and MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS=20_971_520. Keep the existing transform-context identity assertions unchanged. Out: validation (US-002/003), seed/model refusal (US-004), imagesAsNotes and token estimates (US-006), persistent image removal/sidecars (US-007/008), ACP (US-009). Removing image files of messages that compaction dropped; they stay until the transcript is deleted.

**Interface** — `capRequestImages(messages)` accepts the readonly native transcript message array and returns the input array itself if no drop is needed, otherwise a fresh bounded wire array. Use completeWithRecovery and createLoopEventRegistry().register("transform_context", ...) in bun:test to prove the final request boundary is capped but returned messages preserve all images. Oversized pure-function fixtures intentionally exceed facade limits to exercise historical/patched contexts. Prove old-code failures before implementation.

userStories.title: Images in compaction
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Account for image tokens and give compaction summaries text-only image notes rather than image bytes.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

**Approach** — `estimateTokens` adds, per image of a user message, `min(IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE, ceil(width * height / 750))` when both `width` and `height` are present, else `IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE`.

The summarizer never receives image bytes: `imagesAsNotes(messages)` returns messages in which every image of every user message is replaced by the appended line `[image: <mimeType> <width>x<height>]` (or `[image: <mimeType>]` without both dimensions) and `images` is removed. `summarizeAndApply` in `turn-compaction-step.ts` calls `deps.summarize(imagesAsNotes(plan.toSummarize), plan.previousSummary)`.

Every note line this feature appends to a user message's `content` (`[image from an earlier turn dropped from context: ...]`, `[image: ...]`, `[image missing]`) is appended once per image, in image order, joined to the existing `content` with `\n`; when `content` is empty the first line is used with no leading `\n`.

Preserve the existing ceil(content.length/4) text estimate and assistant/tool-result accounting. IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE comes from the shared image-input module and equals 1_600. imagesAsNotes must not mutate its input messages; it is the summary input view, not a transcript rewrite. The shared summarizeAndApply call covers proactive and overflow paths; preserve previousSummary and the existing replacementSummary branch that bypasses the summarizer. Preserve runProactiveCompaction's existing nonfatal summary-error fallback (turn-compaction-step.ts:173-184): with no abort and no expired deadline, a rejected summary returns the original image-bearing messages unchanged rather than persisting the note-only summary view.

**Scope** — In: extend US-005's native/session/image-context.ts, compaction.ts and turn-compaction-step.ts; create image-compaction.test.ts and append estimate cases to existing compaction.test.ts without changing existing assertions. Mirror turn-loop-compaction.test.ts for a real proactive-compaction path. Out: request budget algorithm (US-005), transcript encoding/lifecycle (US-007/008), native model refusal (US-004). Removing image files of messages that compaction dropped; they stay until the transcript is deleted.

**Interface** — `imagesAsNotes(messages)` returns native transcript messages with user images replaced by ordered notes and no images property; `estimateTokens(message)` adds the image estimate to its text result. Test the pure functions and the actual deps.summarize input, including the no-bytes guarantee; show regression tests failing on old code before implementation.

userStories.title: Write images to the transcript sidecar
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist image bytes once per content-addressed sidecar file and store private references in image-bearing transcript JSON.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

**Approach** — The image folder for a transcript file is that file's name with the trailing `.json` replaced by `.images`: the live `<dir>/<session>.transcript.json` uses `<dir>/<session>.transcript.images/`, and a retained `<session>.transcript.failed-<stamp>.json` uses `<session>.transcript.failed-<stamp>.images/`.

The extension table is closed: `image/png` → `png`, `image/jpeg` → `jpg`, `image/gif` → `gif`, `image/webp` → `webp`.

**Write** (the store's `save` and `markTurn`, and `saveTranscript`): every user-message image is written once to `<folder>/<sha256-hex-of-raw-bytes>.<ext>` (an existing file is not rewritten), atomically (a staged temp file in the folder renamed into place, as `writeFileAtomic` in `#src/internal/atomic-write` does for text; widening that helper to bytes is fine), before the JSON document. In the JSON document that image becomes `{ mimeType, ref, width?, height?, source? }` with no `data`. The on-disk `schemaVersion` is `2` when the document holds at least one image; otherwise the document's own `schemaVersion` is written as given (absent stays absent, `1` stays `1`), so an image-free document is written exactly as today and no folder is created. An image whose `mimeType` is not in the extension table makes the write reject with `NaxError` code `TRANSCRIPT_IMAGE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (context `stage: "native-session"`) and nothing is written.

`markTurn` goes through the same read and write, so it re-reads image files and re-hashes them on each call; with content-addressed names nothing is rewritten. The extra reads are accepted.

The memory transcript store keeps images inline, unchanged.

The stored image shape is private to the store module; the rest of nax-agent only sees `ImageAttachment` with `data`.

Image files of messages that compaction later removes stay in the folder until the transcript is deleted (see Out of Scope).

An image file write fails: the save rejects with the underlying error; the transcript file keeps its previous content; no partial image file is left under its final name. Preflight the entire document's MIME declarations before any write, stage images inside their folder, clean failed temporary files, and replace JSON only after image publication. Preserve the original text atomic-write behavior if widening its accepted content to bytes. Recompute disk version per save rather than carrying version 2 forward after images disappear.

Explicit AC18 requires a second save after a staged rename failure to succeed and load to return the original image data. This write-story AC is authoritative: include the minimum successful version-2 round-trip read compatibility necessary to satisfy it without changing TranscriptDoc.schemaVersion?:1. US-008 extends the reader's full invalid/missing/version handling and lifecycle; do not move AC18 or introduce a reverse dependency.

**Scope** — In: create native/session/transcript-images.ts and transcript-images-write.test.ts, wire the shared transcript-store write path used by save/markTurn/saveTranscript, optionally widen internal/atomic-write.ts using its injectable filesystem seam. Out: full safe rehydration, missing-note and folder delete/retain/prune behavior (US-008), memory-store format changes, request capping/compaction (US-005/006). Removing image files of messages that compaction dropped; they stay until the transcript is deleted.

**Interface** — Stored image `{ mimeType, ref, width?, height?, source? }` is private. `TranscriptDoc.schemaVersion` stays `?: 1` in memory: the on-disk `2` never leaves the file store. Public file-store/saveTranscript signatures stay unchanged. Use node:fs/promises and node:crypto, not Bun APIs. Use _*Deps for failure injection and show old-code failures before implementation.

**Goal** — Rehydrate stored images safely and give sidecar folders the same lifecycle as their transcript JSON files.

**Motivation** — The chat UI (feature 2) needs a stable layer to build on: a way to send images, a way to ask whether the current brain reads them, and storage that survives resume.

A document stored with `schemaVersion: 2` is returned with **no `schemaVersion` key**, and a stored `1` (or absent) is returned as stored: version 2 is a disk-format detail of the file store, so the three existing doc-level readers (`historyFromTranscript` in `transcript-identity.ts`, `instruction-session.ts`, `agent-session-resume.ts`), which accept only 1 or absent, need no change.

**Lifecycle**: `deleteTranscript` also removes the live folder; `retainTranscript` renames it to the retained folder name with the same stamp; `pruneRetainedTranscripts` removes the folder of each transcript file it deletes.

`markTurn` goes through the same read and write, so it re-reads image files and re-hashes them on each call; with content-addressed names nothing is rewritten. The extra reads are accepted.

The memory transcript store keeps images inline, unchanged.

The stored image shape is private to the store module; the rest of nax-agent only sees `ImageAttachment` with `data`.

Image files of messages that compaction later removes stay in the folder until the transcript is deleted (see Out of Scope).

The image folder for a transcript file is that file's name with the trailing `.json` replaced by `.images`: the live `<dir>/<session>.transcript.json` uses `<dir>/<session>.transcript.images/`, and a retained `<session>.transcript.failed-<stamp>.json` uses `<session>.transcript.failed-<stamp>.images/`.

The extension table is closed: `image/png` → `png`, `image/jpeg` → `jpg`, `image/gif` → `gif`, `image/webp` → `webp`.

Every note line this feature appends to a user message's `content` (`[image from an earlier turn dropped from context: ...]`, `[image: ...]`, `[image missing]`) is appended once per image, in image order, joined to the existing `content` with `\n`; when `content` is empty the first line is used with no leading `\n`.

Reject invalid refs and MIME before deriving or reading image paths; never read outside the sidecar folder. Missing files, invalid refs and unsupported stored MIME are missing-image notes, not load errors. Remove a user message's images property if every image was dropped. Retained JSON and folder use one generated stamp, and pruning retains the folders corresponding to kept JSON.

**Goal** — Advertise the current ACP agent's image support and send image blocks only on a turn's initial prompt.
